newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol surprised at move on night flight ban.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol surprised at move on night flight ban.

text.p: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol said it was surprised by Friday's verdict by a Dutch court which found that the airport was not permitted to introduce a night ban on noisier aircraft.
The Haarlem Court ruled that such measures could only be taken by the Dutch Transport minister, Annemarie Jorritsma.

On July 23, the airport said that from August 1 noisy aircraft -- including freighters -- such as the McDonnell Douglas DC-10 and various earlier versions of the Boeing 747 would be banned from landing at Schiphol between 2100 to 0400 GMT.
Airport users then appealed to the government to stop the ban but on August 4 the government ruled the ban would go ahead with effect from the next day, August 5.
This resulted in the latest court hearing as a result of moves by the Dutch Air Transport Association (ATAN) and several individual users.
The airport authority also said on Friday that it welcomed Thursday's decision by the minister to declare Schiphol a "coordinated airport" from September 1.

This means that the airport will effectively have an overall noise cap and each airline must stay within its permitted share of the overall level. An independent coordinator will decide on how the slots are shared.

However the airport did say that it was too late to be able to introduce new noise allocations this year and in the short term, Schiphol will have talks with the minister and the aviation industry to discuss measures that will enable it to keep within the noise zones. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
